grammar.title: Presente simple y adverbios de frecuencia
grammar.explanation: El presente simple se usa para rutinas y hábitos. Los adverbios de frecuencia dicen cada cuánto haces algo.

examples: I have breakfast with my family.

rules.rule: Con he / she / it el verbo lleva -s
examples: He goes to work by bus.
I never go to bed late.

rules.rule: El adverbio va antes del verbo (pero después de 'to be')
Preguntas de sí / no: Do / Does + sujeto + verbo?
examples: Do you exercise every day? — Yes, I do. / No, I don't.
I brush my teeth twice a day
I take a shower in the morning
I go to work by bus
I have dinner with my family
I exercise three times a week

grammar.title: Pronombres reflexivos
grammar.explanation: Se usan cuando la persona que hace la acción es la misma que la recibe, o para decir que alguien hizo algo solo, sin ayuda.

rules.rule: Singular: myself, yourself, himself, herself, itself
examples: She looked at herself in the mirror.
my book (posesivo) ≠ I did it myself (reflexivo)
My mother-in-law lives in another city
I have a stepbrother from my mother's new marriage
My niece loves to play with dolls
My husband works as an engineer

grammar.title: Adjetivos comparativos
grammar.explanation: Sirven para comparar dos cosas. La forma depende del largo del adjetivo, y siempre va seguida de 'than'.

rules.rule: Hablar del clima: It is + adjetivo

examples: Don't forget your umbrella, it's rainy.
Rainy days are good for reading.
We can make a snowman on snowy days.
I go to the beach in summer.
I need a jacket, it's cold.
